subject: Electrical Engineering
title: On-Off Control: The Simplest Strategy
description: A quick, practical guide to On-Off Control: The Simplest Strategy.

hook.text: Too cold? Heater on. Warm enough? Heater off. On-off control is dead simple.

buildup.text: The controller has only two states — full power or zero. No in-between.

discovery.text: This causes oscillation around the setpoint. The output constantly overshoots and undershoots.

twist.text: Hysteresis adds a dead band — don't switch off until 23°C, don't switch on until 21°C. Reduces chatter.

climax.text: Refrigerators, room heaters, and basic thermostats use on-off control with hysteresis.

punchline.text: On or off — crude but effective. Add hysteresis and it works surprisingly well.

quiz.question: Why is hysteresis added to on-off controllers?
options: To increase the controller's switching speed
To create a dead band that prevents rapid toggling around the setpoint
To eliminate all overshoot from the system
